requirements.statement: The notification hub's browser title is 'Overview - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and its main heading is 'Overview'.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification in Design Release 2.1, named Overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-002 and trace-animals-fit-p4-002 show the title and h1 'Overview' today.

requirements.statement: Each notification has its own hub address (under /live-animals/notifications/{reference}), rather than one hub page for whichever notification is in the session.
requirements.why: The real service stores many notifications per trader, so the hub must say which one it shows; the prototype holds a single notification in its session and cannot express this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-001 serves the hub at /notifications/{journeyId} under the live-animals set; c-notification-hub-002 keeps it over the prototype's single /notification-hub route.

requirements.statement: Above the 'Overview' heading the hub shows the notification's status as a tag ('Draft' until it is submitted) followed by the notification reference.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are on and what state it is in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-004 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 show the journey strip with a 'Draft' tag and the reference above the heading today.

requirements.statement: A live-animals notification's reference reads 'GBN-AG-26-' followed by six upper-case letters or digits, unique among the trader's notifications, and it exists from the first time the hub is shown.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the reference on a fresh notification in this form.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p4-004 shows every reference the real service created in the GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX form, from the first page of the notification. The real service creates the reference with the record rather than on opening the hub.

requirements.statement: Opening the hub leaves the notification saved as a draft: nothing a trader has answered is lost by leaving from the hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the draft when the hub opens; the real service already saves each page's answers to the notification record as it goes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-044-m1 shows every saved page committing to the stored notification (the concurrency token rises per save), so the draft is already saved whenever the hub shows.

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended (status 'Amend'), the hub's status line also shows a 'Cancel amend' link-style button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers cancelling an amendment from the status line on every page that shows it, the hub included.
requirements.deltaNote: The real hub's strip shows only the tag and reference (repo-frontend-p4-004); cancel amend is offered today only from the review page and the dashboard.

requirements.statement: The hub has no back link; the ways off it are the 'Return to dashboard' button and the service navigation.
requirements.why: The hub is the top of the notification, not a step in it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-005 and trace-animals-fit-p4-005 show no back link on the hub today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a 'Your commodities' heading (h2) above the commodity total cards, on every visit, including before any commodity is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the hub with the consignment totals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-006 and trace-animals-fit-p4-007 show the 'Your commodities' h2 from the first visit today.

requirements.statement: For a live-animals notification the first card shows the total number of animals, labelled 'Animals' with the caption 'Total number of animals in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the animals total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-007 and trace-animals-fit-p4-008 show the 'Animals' label and caption verbatim today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows a card for the total number of packages, labelled 'Packages/boxes' with the caption 'Total number of packages in this consignment'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for the packages total card.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-008 and trace-animals-fit-p4-009 show the 'Packages/boxes' label and caption verbatim today.

requirements.statement: The animals and packages totals add up only the counts entered on every commodity line that are positive numbers; blank, zero, negative or non-numeric values add nothing, and a card reads '0' when its total is not above zero.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only positive entries, so a card never shows a negative or odd total.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-010: today any finite number counts towards the total (only blank or non-numeric values count as zero), so a negative count would lower the total; DR2.1 adds only positive counts. Summing across lines and reading 0 before any line exists already hold (repo-frontend-p4-009, repo-frontend-p4-011).

requirements.statement: When a notification holds only germinal products, the hub shows the 'Packages/boxes' card and a net weight card labelled 'Kilograms' with the caption 'Total weight of packages in this consignment', instead of the 'Animals' card.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted by packages and weight, not by animals, in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hub always shows the Animals and Packages/boxes cards (trace-animals-fit-p4-008); it has no weight card. Depends on the commodities area offering germinal products.

requirements.statement: The 'Kilograms' card shows '0' when the total weight is not a positive number, a whole number as entered, and otherwise the total rounded to 3 decimal places (for example '2.5').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's rule for displaying the net weight total.

requirements.statement: Each commodity total card is a static panel (no link or button) that reads the number, then the label, then the caption; the cards sit side by side on a wide screen and stack with no horizontal scrolling on a 360px screen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the totals as value, label and caption tiles; the real hub already draws them that way from GOV.UK design tokens.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-012 to p4-016 and trace-animals-fit-p4-014 to p4-018 show static number-label-caption panels, side by side and stacking on a small screen, today.

requirements.statement: Assistive technology can move by region on the hub: each total card is a region labelled 'Animals summary', 'Packages summary' (and a matching label for the Kilograms card), and the 'Your commodities' block, the task list and each numbered section are regions named by their own heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks these regions up for screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the task list is headed 'Notification tasklist' (h2), below the commodity totals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heading for the task list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-017 and trace-animals-fit-p4-020 render the 'Notification tasklist' h2 today (DR1 already landed it, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-046).

requirements.statement: For a notification, the task list has exactly six numbered sections with h3 headings, in this order: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Documents', '5. Consignment parties', '6. Contact address', and nothing after them (no review task row).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 section structure for the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-018 and trace-animals-fit-p4-021 show the six sections, verbatim and in order, with nothing after them, today.

requirements.statement: The third row of section 1 reads 'Main import reason' (not 'Main reason for import'), in English and in the Welsh copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 renamed the task; DR1 named it after its own prototype, which is not a judgement departing from the design, so Design Release 2.1 wins.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-025 and trace-animals-fit-p4-028 show the row titled 'Main reason for import' today; the Welsh machine draft (repo-frontend-p4-053) needs the matching key changed.

requirements.statement: Section 1 holds, in order, 'Where is this consignment coming from?', 'What are you importing?' and the main import reason row; there is no separate exit details row, and the import reason row is complete only once the reason and any follow-up it reveals are answered (Re-entry alone completes it).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows three rows in section 1; DR1 already folded exit details into the import reason task.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-019 and trace-animals-fit-p4-028 show the three rows in this order today, and DR1 removed the exit details row (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-026); only the third row's title changes (req-notification-hub-018).

requirements.statement: 'Commodity details' is its own row, first in section 2, shown from a fresh notification as 'To do'; it reads 'Complete' once the number of animals (and packages where asked) is saved for every chosen commodity, while 'What are you importing?' reads 'Complete' as soon as a commodity is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 splits choosing the commodity from giving its numbers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-020/p4-041 and trace-animals-fit-p4-032 to p4-034 show the separate row, first in section 2, live with 'To do' from the start, as DR2.1 does (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p11-032); this settles the open DR1 gating call (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-043) as the status quo.

requirements.statement: 'Identification details' shows in section 2, between 'Commodity details' and 'Additional details', only when a chosen commodity needs animal identifiers, and is absent otherwise (for example before a commodity is chosen, or for poultry).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for identifiers only for the species that need them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-036 and trace-e2e-p13-022/023 show the row absent until a commodity carrying identifiers is chosen, then placed between Commodity details and Additional details. Which commodities carry identifiers, and what makes the row complete, belong to the animal-identification area.

requirements.statement: 'Additional details' shows in section 2 only when the additional animal details page applies: it is shown for live animals and left out when the notification holds only germinal products.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 drops the additional animal details task for germinal products, which have no animal certification or unweaned question.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-035 makes only Identification details and Transit countries conditional; 'Additional details' is always shown today (trace-e2e-p13-021, trace-animals-fit-p4-042). Depends on the commodities area offering germinal products.

requirements.statement: Section 3 always shows 'Arrival details', which opens even before a commodity is chosen, and 'Transport details'; each reads 'Complete' once its answers are saved.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 rows for arrival and transport.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-021 and trace-e2e-p13-024 show both rows in section 3 today, and trace-animals-fit-p4-044/045 show Arrival details opening and completing before a commodity is chosen.

requirements.statement: 'Transit countries' shows in section 3, between 'Arrival details' and 'Transport details', only when transit countries are required for the notification (shown for poultry and germinal products, not for pet cats), and reads 'Complete' once at least one transit country is selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 decides from the notification whether transit countries are owed, and shows the row only then.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the row appears once arrival details are saved, even with no commodity chosen and the transit page skipped (trace-animals-fit-p4-047/048); DR2.1 shows it only when transit countries are required. The rule that decides when they are required belongs to the arrival-and-transit area.

requirements.statement: For a notification, section '4. Documents' holds the single row 'Upload documents', which reads 'Complete' once at least one document is uploaded and otherwise 'To do', and never stops the notification reaching review or submission.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats documents as optional.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-022 and trace-animals-fit-p4-050/051 show the single 'Upload documents' row, 'To do' while the rest is complete, with the review still open; trace-e2e-p13-033 shows the notification submittable without documents.

requirements.statement: Section 'Consignment parties' holds the single row 'Roles and addresses', with the hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination' under its link; the row covers the CPH number too, and it is the only row with a hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 row and hint for the consignment parties.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-026/p4-046 and trace-animals-fit-p4-052 to p4-054 show the row, its hint verbatim, and CPH folded into it today.

requirements.statement: Section 'Contact address' holds the single row 'Contact address for this consignment', which reads 'Complete' once a contact address is chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 row for the contact address.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-024 and trace-animals-fit-p4-055 show the row, verbatim, completing once a contact is chosen, today.

requirements.statement: Each hub row shows one of two status tags only: a green 'Complete' when the task is finished and its saved answers still pass their page's rules, otherwise a blue 'To do'; there is no 'In progress', optional or other state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses exactly two task states on the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-029 to p4-031 and trace-animals-fit-p4-024 show only green 'Complete' and blue 'To do' today.

requirements.statement: Every row the hub shows is a link the trader can open at any time, in any order: no row is locked or shown as 'Cannot start yet', and a row that does not apply is left off the hub rather than shown locked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader start any task in any order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-027/p4-033/p4-034 and trace-animals-fit-p4-026 show every shown row as a link, none 'Cannot start yet', and inapplicable conditional rows removed, today.

requirements.statement: The hub's task list is built from the GOV.UK Task list component, one per section, with each row's status (and the Roles and addresses hint) tied to its link by aria-describedby, so a screen reader moving by links hears the task, its hint and its status.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom markup does not tie status or hint to the link, which fails screen-reader users; the GOV.UK component gives the same look and meets the accessibility regulations the real service must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p4-023 and trace-e2e-p13-030-m1 show GOV.UK task lists with aria-describedby status (and hint) ids today; c-notification-hub-003 keeps them over the prototype's custom markup.

requirements.statement: A new notification goes from choosing the notification type to the origin page, and the first hub a trader reaches already shows 'Where is this consignment coming from?' as 'Complete'; reaching the hub ends the guided first pass through the journey.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends a new live-animals notification to the origin page first, not to the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-055 and trace-animals-fit-p4-027 show a new notification held on the origin page, so the first hub has origin Complete. The prototype shows an all-'To do' hub only when its URL is typed directly, which the real per-notification hub does not need to copy.

requirements.statement: When a trader opens a task from a hub row, 'Save and continue' saves and returns them to the hub once that row's own pages are done, rather than carrying on into the next row's pages: for example the main import reason returns to the hub instead of going on to Additional details, and Arrival details returns to the hub instead of going on to Transit countries and Transport details.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 a task opened from the hub (from=hub) comes back to the hub when saved, so the trader chooses what to do next.
requirements.deltaNote: Today, from the hub, Save and continue moves on through the rest of the task group before returning: import reason goes on to Additional details (trace-animals-fit-p4-030) and port of entry goes on to transit countries and transporters (trace-animals-fit-p4-046, trace-e2e-p13-041). Pages inside one row (addresses then CPH number) still run on to each other.

requirements.statement: A task page opened from the hub has a 'Back' link to the hub and ends with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' that saves and goes to the hub, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that goes to the hub without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives every task page reached from the hub these ways back to it; DR1's rule (b) already limits the three controls to pages the overview links to.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-037 to p13-039 and p13-043 show the Back link to the hub and the three exits on task pages today.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub ends with a primary 'Review and submit' button that opens the review page, always shown and active whatever the task statuses; submitting is still gated on the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers the review at any time and names what is outstanding there.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-050 and trace-animals-fit-p4-059 show 'Review and submit' as the primary button, opening the review page with only the origin answered, today.

requirements.statement: For a notification, the hub's secondary button is 'Return to dashboard', after 'Review and submit' in the same button group, going to the dashboard.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's way off the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-052 and trace-animals-fit-p4-061 show the secondary 'Return to dashboard' going to the dashboard today.

requirements.statement: The hub shows only its main and secondary buttons: there is no 'Save as template' button on it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no save-as-template action on the hub.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-064 shows the button group holding only 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard' today.

requirements.statement: The hub has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA accessibility violations, whether it shows zero totals, a commodity with numbers owed, or non-zero totals.
requirements.why: The real service must meet the accessibility regulations; the hub already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-067/p4-068 and trace-animals-fit-p4-019 show axe passing on the hub in each state today.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the status tag reads 'Template' and the template's name is shown beside it in place of a notification reference.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reuses the hub to build a template and labels it as one.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the task list is headed 'Template tasklist'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heading for the template task list.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the Documents section is left out and the sections after it are renumbered '4. Consignment parties' and '5. Contact address'.
requirements.why: A template holds no shipment-specific documents in Design Release 2.1.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the primary button reads 'Review template' and opens the review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends a template to review rather than submission.

requirements.statement: When the hub is showing a template being created, the secondary button reads 'Return to manage templates' and goes to the templates list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's way off a template's hub.

requirements.statement: A 'Save template' button going straight to saving the template is not built on the hub.
requirements.why: The prototype shows it only outside Design Release 2.1; in Design Release 2.1 every template creation gets 'Review template' instead, and the goal is Design Release 2.1.

conflicts.about: Whether the hub's 'Cancel amend' link does anything: DR2.1 shows it on the hub during an amendment but does not put the cancel-amendment modal on the hub page.

positions.says: While the status is 'Amend', the status line shows a 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel amendment modal.
The hub page does not include the cancel amendment modal, so the button has nothing to open there.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype contradicts itself on the hub; nothing ranks the two readings, and they build different things (a working link or none).
conflicts.question: During an amendment, should the hub's status line offer a working 'Cancel amend', or leave it off because DR2.1 gives it nothing to open there?
conflicts.default: The hub shows 'Cancel amend' during an amendment, and it opens the same cancel-amendment confirmation the review page uses.

conflicts.about: The hub's address: one /notification-hub page for the session's notification, or one hub per stored notification.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype.
The hub is reached at GET /notification-hub, for the one notification held in the session.
The hub is served per notification at /notifications/{journeyId}.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the real service persists many notifications per trader, which the prototype's session cannot express, so the hub keeps its per-notification address. What the hub shows still follows DR2.1.

conflicts.about: The hub task list markup: DR2.1's custom tasklist with status and hint not tied to the link, or the GOV.UK Task list component.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
The task list is custom app-notification-hub-* markup rather than the GOV.UK Task list component.
A task's status tag and hint are not tied to its link, so a screen reader moving by links hears only the task name.
Each section is a GOV.UK Task list with the status (and hint) tied to the link by aria-describedby.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the real service must meet the public sector accessibility regulations, a constraint a prototype does not carry. The GOV.UK Task list gives the same visible rows, tags and hint as DR2.1, so the look and copy follow DR2.1 and the markup stays the GOV.UK component.
